speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash on your trunk and extremities, and when did you first notice it?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash have a "slapped cheek" appearance on the face, and are there lacy, reticular patterns on the trunk and extremities? Has she recently been exposed to anyone with similar symptoms or attended school during an outbreak?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the characteristic "slapped cheek" facial rash sparing the perioral area and the subsequent lacy, reticular rash on the trunk and extremities following mild prodromal symptoms, the clinical presentation is classic for Erythema Infectiosum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
